assertions.description: AbortController.abort(reason) stores the exact reason value on signal.reason and throwIfAborted() throws that same value by identity.
assertions.test: (() => { const sentinel = new Error('conf-sentinel'); const c = new AbortController(); c.abort(sentinel); if (c.signal.reason !== sentinel) return false; try { c.signal.throwIfAborted(); return false; } catch (e) { return e === sentinel; } })()

assertions.description: Aborting a fetch whose promise is still pending rejects that promise with the exact reason passed to abort(), not a substitute. Runs a real aborted fetch inside a dedicated worker so the page's own network log stays free of the intentional cancellation.
assertions.test: (async () => { const abs = new URL('/features', location.href).href; const body = "(async () => { try { const sentinel = new Error('conf-pending-sentinel'); const c = new AbortController(); const p = fetch(" + JSON.stringify(abs) + ", { signal: c.signal }); c.abort(sentinel); try { await p; postMessage(false); } catch (e) { postMessage(e === sentinel); } } catch (e) { postMessage({ error: String(e) }); } })();"; const w = new Worker(URL.createObjectURL(new Blob([body], { type: 'text/javascript' }))); try { const r = await new Promise((res, rej) => { w.onmessage = (e) => res(e.data); w.onerror = (e) => rej(new Error(e.message || 'worker error')); setTimeout(() => rej(new Error('worker timeout')), 8000); }); if (r && r.error) throw new Error(r.error); return r === true; } finally { w.terminate(); } })()

assertions.description: Aborting with no argument rejects the pending fetch promise with a DOMException whose name is AbortError (the spec-minted default reason). Runs inside a dedicated worker.
assertions.test: (async () => { const abs = new URL('/features', location.href).href; const body = "(async () => { try { const c = new AbortController(); const p = fetch(" + JSON.stringify(abs) + ", { signal: c.signal }); c.abort(); try { await p; postMessage(false); } catch (e) { postMessage(e instanceof DOMException && e.name === 'AbortError'); } } catch (e) { postMessage({ error: String(e) }); } })();"; const w = new Worker(URL.createObjectURL(new Blob([body], { type: 'text/javascript' }))); try { const r = await new Promise((res, rej) => { w.onmessage = (e) => res(e.data); w.onerror = (e) => rej(new Error(e.message || 'worker error')); setTimeout(() => rej(new Error('worker timeout')), 8000); }); if (r && r.error) throw new Error(r.error); return r === true; } finally { w.terminate(); } })()

assertions.description: After the fetch promise has resolved, aborting while the body is still streaming rejects a pending body reader.read() with the exact abort reason — the contract Chrome 153 ships; pre-153 Chromium substitutes a generic AbortError and fails this. Runs a real chunked fetch inside a dedicated worker.
assertions.test: (async () => { const abs = new URL('/v152/renewed-html-insertion-streaming-methods/html-stream?chunks=4&delay=300', location.href).href; const body = "(async () => { try { const c = new AbortController(); const res = await fetch(" + JSON.stringify(abs) + ", { signal: c.signal }); if (!res.ok) { postMessage({ error: 'streaming endpoint unavailable: HTTP ' + res.status }); return; } const reader = res.body.getReader(); await reader.read(); const sentinel = new Error('conf-midstream-sentinel'); const pending = reader.read(); c.abort(sentinel); try { await pending; postMessage(false); } catch (e) { postMessage(e === sentinel); } } catch (e) { postMessage({ error: String(e) }); } })();"; const w = new Worker(URL.createObjectURL(new Blob([body], { type: 'text/javascript' }))); try { const r = await new Promise((res, rej) => { w.onmessage = (e) => res(e.data); w.onerror = (e) => rej(new Error(e.message || 'worker error')); setTimeout(() => rej(new Error('worker timeout')), 10000); }); if (r && r.error) throw new Error(r.error); return r === true; } finally { w.terminate(); } })()

assertions.description: After the fetch promise has resolved, aborting while Response.text() is buffering the body rejects that text() promise with the exact abort reason (Chrome 153 contract; pre-153 Chromium fails this). Runs inside a dedicated worker.
assertions.test: (async () => { const abs = new URL('/v152/renewed-html-insertion-streaming-methods/html-stream?chunks=4&delay=300', location.href).href; const body = "(async () => { try { const c = new AbortController(); const res = await fetch(" + JSON.stringify(abs) + ", { signal: c.signal }); if (!res.ok) { postMessage({ error: 'streaming endpoint unavailable: HTTP ' + res.status }); return; } const sentinel = { code: 'CONF-TEXT-SENTINEL' }; const settled = res.text().then(() => ({ resolved: true }), (e) => ({ resolved: false, forwarded: e === sentinel })); await new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, 350)); c.abort(sentinel); const out = await settled; postMessage(out.resolved === false && out.forwarded === true); } catch (e) { postMessage({ error: String(e) }); } })();"; const w = new Worker(URL.createObjectURL(new Blob([body], { type: 'text/javascript' }))); try { const r = await new Promise((res, rej) => { w.onmessage = (e) => res(e.data); w.onerror = (e) => rej(new Error(e.message || 'worker error')); setTimeout(() => rej(new Error('worker timeout')), 10000); }); if (r && r.error) throw new Error(r.error); return r === true; } finally { w.terminate(); } })()

assertions.description: A TimeoutError DOMException minted by AbortSignal.timeout() propagates to a pending mid-stream body read as a TimeoutError, not a generic AbortError — forwarding applies to every reason, not just user-supplied ones. Runs inside a dedicated worker.
assertions.test: (async () => { const abs = new URL('/v152/renewed-html-insertion-streaming-methods/html-stream?chunks=6&delay=400', location.href).href; const body = "(async () => { try { const signal = AbortSignal.timeout(700); const res = await fetch(" + JSON.stringify(abs) + ", { signal }); if (!res.ok) { postMessage({ error: 'streaming endpoint unavailable: HTTP ' + res.status }); return; } const reader = res.body.getReader(); try { for (;;) { const st = await reader.read(); if (st.done) { postMessage(false); return; } } } catch (e) { postMessage(e instanceof DOMException && e.name === 'TimeoutError'); } } catch (e) { postMessage({ error: String(e) }); } })();"; const w = new Worker(URL.createObjectURL(new Blob([body], { type: 'text/javascript' }))); try { const r = await new Promise((res, rej) => { w.onmessage = (e) => res(e.data); w.onerror = (e) => rej(new Error(e.message || 'worker error')); setTimeout(() => rej(new Error('worker timeout')), 12000); }); if (r && r.error) throw new Error(r.error); return r === true; } finally { w.terminate(); } })()
